entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Sancho of Aragon, Infante of Aragon and Archbishop of Toledo, played a pivotal role in the tumultuous landscape of medieval Spain. Born in 1250, he rose through the ranks of the Aragonese nobility to become a prominent figure in the kingdom's religious and political hierarchy. Sancho's significance lies in his leadership during the Moorish reconquest of Toledo, where he was killed in action on October 28, 1275. His legacy extends to the establishment of the Toledo Cathedral, which remains an iconic symbol of the city's rich cultural heritage. The devastating impact of his death on the Aragonese monarchy cannot be overstated, as it marked the beginning of a period of instability that would shape the kingdom's future for centuries to come. As a testament to his enduring influence, Sancho's name continues to be invoked in discussions of Spanish history and politics to this day.
